feedback: This candidate is the iteration 3 design (best so far, 471.07) with one change: controller.base_speed from 1.1 to 1.0. Iteration 3 finished the oval 20 of 20 at a mean of 1.96 s, so the time limit has room. Its s-bend still ended off track in 17 of 20 runs with mean max_error 0.0598 m, right at the 0.06 m limit. Its slalom had 0 finishes, progress 0.10 and max_error 0.0617 m, with 0 line-loss events, so line loss is not the cause. Across iterations 0, 1 and 3, lowering speed has reduced bend max_error each time (1.6 to 1.3 to 1.1), while iteration 2 showed that the sensor-spacing change was the source of its collapse. This candidate keeps the iteration 3 geometry and kp 1.6, kd 0.5, ki 0, sensor_weights -2..2 and last_direction, so the race isolates speed. The main risk is that at 1.0 the robot is too slow to reach progress 0.995 on the slalom or stalls, which would show as low progress with no off-track end. Nothing here is obviously broken, and the change is a single, well-supported step, so it should be raced. Read the telemetry as follows. If the oval completion_time exceeds about 2.8 s, return toward 1.05. If the s-bend and slalom still show max_error at or above 0.06 m at speed 1.0, the next lever is kd (for example 0.5 to 0.7), since kd was only varied together with other changes in iteration 2. If the slalom stalls with progress flat, try 1.05 before changing gains.
requested_changes: If the s-bend and slalom still reach max_error at or above 0.06 m at base_speed 1.0, raise controller.kd from 0.5 toward 0.7 with everything else fixed, since speed alone has not yet cleared the limit and kd has not been isolated.
If the oval completion_time rises above about 2.8 s, or the slalom stalls with progress flat, set controller.base_speed to 1.05, the midpoint between the best-scoring 1.1 and this 1.0 run.

Keep geometry.sensor_positions at the iteration 1 and 3 layout (x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps, y 0.05). The iteration 2 change to 0.04 m spacing and y 0.07 scored 62.76 with 2.8 line-loss events on the oval, so do not reintroduce it.
